messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High latency observed for tenant OpalRidge in eu3 dedicated pool (incident id: INC-2026-0712-OPR). p99 spike detected; auto-page to SRE rotation. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/INC-2026-0712-OPR :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: I’m on it. seeing p95 ~ 1.2s -> p99 ~ 3.8s starting ~ 2026-03-17T09:28:00Z. error rate still ~0.3% but tail latency up. Affected pool: eu3-dedicated-42, tenant: opalridge-prod (customer_id: c-0912).

kevin.h: ping — is this cache-thrashing or GC? cores on gpu nodes at 94-98%?

sre-oncall: GPU utilization high, LRU evictions spiking, KV cache miss rate jumped 6x. Looks like request mix changed (longer seqs). No infra OOMs.

platform_lead: Two immediate mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant qps throttle to cap opalridge to safe baseline; 2) prepare tenant isolation (evict to warm spare) if throttle doesn't bring p99 down in 5m.

aya: I can push throttle now. Suggested command: `POST /admin/tenants/opалridge/actions` body `{ "action": "throttle", "qps": 6 }` — will that be fine?

kevin.h: 6 qps conservative but okay. note: eviction will wipe in-flight KV cache and cause transient higher latency for those sessions. If we can reroute new sessions to eu2 warm spare that’s safer.

solutions_eng: We have a warm spare pool in eu2 with compatible model variants. If we enable route override for opalridge to eu2, model variant must be `redwood-compat-v1-small` for capacity. Expect lower quality but better latency.

maria_g: I’ll notify the customer (OpalRidge SRE) that we’re throttling and may fail over some traffic to eu2 for stability. Draft: "We’re actively mitigating a p99 latency spike impacting your eu3 dedicated pool. Short-term throttle applied; we may shift new traffic to eu2 to restore SLA. We’ll update in 10 mins." ok? :email:

platform_lead: Go ahead. Also roll a temporary canary: `route override opalridge -> eu2 (variant redwood-compat-v1-small) weight 20%` then increase if stable.

aya: throttle applied at 09:31:10Z. qps cap = 6. Monitoring...

ops-bot: METRIC UPDATE: p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 2.1s after throttle (09:33:40Z). CPU/GPU utilization down to ~82%.

kevin.h: Good sign. Recommend route override now to take pressure off pool while we investigate root cause of increased sequence lengths.

platform_lead: Executed route override to eu2 at 09:35:08Z, 20% traffic. watch for error delta and quality regressions.

solutions_eng: Observing request content — several large batched prompts from a recently deployed OpalRidge feature. Flagging for their app team to reduce batch sizes.

maria_g: Notified customer at 09:36Z. They acknowledge and say they’ll push a rollback to previous prompt format. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: ALERT: Quality regression detector fired (minor) on eu2 variant at 09:40:00Z — expected for smaller model. No errors.

sre-oncall: Increasing eu2 weight to 40% to relieve eu3, keeping throttle. p99 now 1.0s on eu2, 1.8s on eu3 at 09:42:30Z.

kevin.h: With traffic partially moved and throttle in place, we should run a tenant audit for long-sequence traffic patterns and set a longer-term quota. Opening follow-up ticket: TKT-2026-OPR-01.

platform_lead: Agreed. For immediate closure, will continue to monitor for 30m, keep CS comms active, and coordinate with customer rollback. If stable for 30m, we revert route weights and remove throttle gradually.

maria_g: Customer confirms rollback in progress at 09:48Z. They expect new deploy in ~15m.

ops-bot: METRIC UPDATE: p99 global for opalridge back under 1.2s at 09:55:12Z. Error rate normal.

aya: Removing throttle at 09:58:00Z, and scaling route override back to 10% while they finish rollback.

sre-oncall: Confirming stability window — p99 steady ~1.1s over last 7m. I’m going to close the immediate incident and keep monitoring. Will file post-incident notes.

maria_g: I’ll send post-incident message to customer summarizing actions and recommended changes (smaller batch sizes, tenant qps guardrails, alert tuning).

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-2026-0712-OPR marked resolved at 10:05:45Z by sre-oncall. Summary: transient spike caused by tenant-side change increasing sequence lengths -> throttle + partial failover -> customer rollback -> restored. Follow-up: TKT-2026-OPR-01 for quotas and long-term mitigations. :white_check_mark:
